text: During descent I was reprogramming the FMS and missed the ATC altitude call-out. We descended 400 ft below assigned altitude before I noticed.
Weather was deteriorating and I decided to continue the visual approach instead of requesting the ILS, even though I was not fully confident.
I knowingly skipped the checklist item for cabin pressurization because we were running behind schedule.
I misjudged the distance to the runway threshold in low visibility and flared too early.
During taxi I forgot to switch to ground frequency after landing, a routine step I usually do automatically.
I chose to depart despite a known minor hydraulic warning, believing it was not critical.
I intentionally exceeded the sterile cockpit rule by discussing unrelated topics below 10,000 ft.
In heavy rain I misread the runway edge lights and briefly drifted off centerline.
I was fatigued and missed a radio call from ATC, a step I would normally catch.
I decided to continue the approach below minimums, judging I could see enough of the runway.
